target_customer: Developer tool and SaaS companies whose users need to run custom code (for example on webhooks) and that did not want to build a serverless platform themselves.
problem: Building a secure serverless platform that packages and runs customers' code takes months and an infrastructure team, and AWS Lambda has timeout and protocol limits.
business_model: Usage based API for hosting customer code, sold to developer platforms
product_category: Developer infrastructure, serverless code hosting API

founders.name: Jessie Young
prior_employers: AWS (senior engineer, call center AI analytics and NLP)

competitors.name: AWS Lambda
competitors.what: Serverless functions; the launch post says it limits timeouts and lacks protocols like gRPC

competitors.name: Heroku
competitors.what: Platform as a service; the launch post compares building this platform to building your own Heroku

technical_complexity.rationale: A multi tenant system that builds images, runs untrusted customer code securely and returns logs and metrics is hard for a two person team, though both founders came from AWS.

defensibility.rationale: Cloud vendors and well funded startups offered similar primitives, and the product could be replicated or replaced by incumbent features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cloud providers already offered functions and container run services; no source describes the company being copied or bought.

market_need_then: The launch post cites an early customer that gave up on an in house serverless system and launched on Cakework in about a week and a SaaS tool whose users run custom code on webhooks.

branding.domain_note: cakework.com is now an archived wedding blog (Cake Work), unrelated to the startup; the startup's own domain history was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain pitch: 'Build your own serverless platform in days instead of months'.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand beyond the YC launch post and aggregator listings; the name collides with cake and wedding terms.

outcome_analysis: Cakework was a two person YC Winter 2023 team of former AWS engineers selling a serverless hosting API to developer platforms, with early access customers but no public traction numbers. The YC directory lists it as inactive and a Wayback copy shows its domain later served an unrelated blog, but no shutdown announcement or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. The failure factors are an inference from the crowded cloud infrastructure market and the absence of any reported follow on funding, not a stated reason.
notes: Aggregators (CB Insights, VCBacked, Extruct) list 500 thousand dollars from Y Combinator as a convertible note or pre seed in early 2023; this matches YC's standard deal and is not recorded as a round. Exit type is shutdown on the basis of the YC Inactive status only; the date is unknown. A StartupIntros page about a Jessie Young at an HR platform with a 4 million seed is probably a different person. Competitor list is from the company's own launch post (undated, early 2023); a StackShare page lists many alternatives without dates. Searches found no shutdown, pivot or successor venture for either founder.
